properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 11 at 1:06PM CDT by NWS Memphis TN
properties.description:
At 105 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Marianna, or near Wall Doxey State Park. This thunderstorm was nearly
stationary.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Holly Springs, Wall Doxey State Park, Red Banks, Marianna, Waterford,
Galena, Mack, Mahon, Higdon, Gilton, and Waites.

This includes Interstate 22 in Mississipppi between mile markers 20
and 36.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 11 at 1:04PM CDT by NWS Huntsville AL
properties.description:
At 104 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Moulton. This thunderstorm was nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Decatur, Hartselle, Moulton, Speake, Neel, Basham, Wren, and eastern
Bankhead National Forest.
properties.instruction:
Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued September 11 at 2:03PM EDT until September 11 at 3:30PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Apalachee Bay or Coastal Waters From Keaton Beach to Ochlockonee
River Fl out to 20 Nm...
Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20
Nm...
Coastal Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola out 20 NM...
Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...
Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 330 PM EDT/230 PM CDT/.

* At 203 PM EDT/103 PM CDT/, severe thunderstorms capable of
producing waterspouts were located along a line extending from near
St George Island to 6 nm west of K Tower, moving east at 5 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
O Tower, Apalachicola, C Tower, Cape San Blas, St George Island,
and K Tower.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Move to safe harbor immediately as gusty winds and high waves are
expected.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.
properties.area: Apalachee Bay or Coastal Waters From Keaton Beach to Ochlockonee River Fl out to 20 Nm; Coastal Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola out 20 NM; Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20 Nm; Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM; Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 11 at 1:53PM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
At 153 PM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Cross, moving east at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Bonneau, Northern Lake Moultrie, Bonneau Beach and Cross Cross
Roads.
properties.instruction:
Boaters on Lake Moultrie should seek safe harbor immediately. If
caught on the open water, stay as low as possible and wear a personal
flotation device. Remember, if you can hear thunder you are at risk
for being struck by lightning.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 11 at 1:48PM EDT by NWS Peachtree City GA
properties.description:
At 148 PM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was over Mountain Hill, or 8
miles west of Hamilton, moving northeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Up to 40 mph wind, frequent cloud to ground lightning and
heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect minor damage to tree limbs and blowing around of
light, unsecured objects. Heavy rain may cause temporary
street flooding especially in poor drainage areas.

Locations impacted include...
Hamilton, Pine Mountain, Pine Mountain-Callaway Gardens, Shiloh,
Mountain Hill, F.D. Roosevelt State Park, Pine Mountain Valley,
Mulberry Grove, and Whitesville-Pine Lake.
properties.instruction:
People outdoors should seek shelter immediately. If you can hear
thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning. Motorists
should slow down and be prepared for possible loss of control due to
hydroplaning.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 11 at 1:17PM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
Showers and thunderstorms will continue to expand near Lake Moultrie
and eastern portions of Lake Marion through mid-afternoon. These
thunderstorms will be capable of producing gusty winds, locally heavy
rainfall reducing visibility 1 NM or less and cloud-to-water
lightning. Mariners are encouraged to seek safe harbor.
properties.instruction:
Boaters on Lake Moultrie and the eastern portions of Lake Marion
should seek safe harbor immediately. If caught on the open water,
stay as low as possible and wear a personal flotation device.
Remember, if you can hear thunder you are at risk for being struck by
lightning.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued September 11 at 12:14PM CDT until September 11 at 2:15PM CDT by NWS Birmingham AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Barbour County in southeastern Alabama...
Southeastern Russell County in southeastern Alabama...

* WHEN...Until 215 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1214 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Lakepoint Resort State Park, Twin Springs, Fort Mitchell Activity
Center and Uchee Creek.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Gadsden County in Big Bend Florida...

* WHEN...Until 315 PM EDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 11 at 9:20AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 affecting DeSoto County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Horse Creek near Arcadia at SR 72.

* WHEN...From late Sunday night until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, The access road to Hidden Oak is
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Friday the stage was 7.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Monday morning and continue rising to 12.2 feet Monday morning.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.2
feet on 11/24/1997.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 930 PM EDT.
